ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account flag on the driver.

rejected_claims.reason: Presence within 200 m (38 m closest approach, first inside 200 m at 13:01:10) satisfies NS-1 (ii) only; it does not satisfy NS-1 (iii), which requires more than 3 minutes inside the radius from the arrival indication, and only 2 min 55 s is recorded after the 13:02:45 tap [F1][F2][F6][NS-1].

The 13:02:25–13:05:40 stationary spell of 3 min 15 s at 40 m is not the measure NS-1 (iii) prescribes; the wait must run from the arrival indication at 13:02:45, after which only 2 min 55 s elapsed before cancellation [F3][F6][NS-1].
The rider's non-boarding is not one of the three cumulative NS-1 conditions; the fee can stand only if (i), (ii) and (iii) are all met, and (iii) fails on the system records [F4][F6][NS-1][NS-2].

The driver's statement and clean 90-day profile are a statement and a profile fact; statements lose to system records and profiles cannot decide a case alone, and the GPS/timeline data contradict the asserted >3-minute post-arrival wait [F12][F17][F6][NS-1].
The driver's $4.50 share is contingent on a validly arising fee; since NS-1 (iii) fails, the fee does not arise and the $6.61 must be refunded under NS-2 [F8][F6][NS-2].

Partially rejected as framed: the rider's own 2 min 55 s post-tap figure is accepted as the controlling interval, but the claim that the tap element is unmet is rejected because the tap at 13:02:45 with 41 m proximity satisfies NS-1 (i) and (ii) [F6][F1][NS-1].
Profile facts (3.9-year account, 4.81 rating, 0 disputes) cannot decide the case alone and are not needed here; the refund rests on the failed NS-1 (iii) wait element [F16][NS-1][NS-2].
Agreed as to outcome — no flag is warranted because the GPS places the driver inside the pickup radius at the tap, so NS-2's false-tap flag condition is not triggered [F1][F6][NS-2].
